trial_name.text: Emory University study R01 (re-analyzed as BED001), published by Schuster et al, J Urol 2014

citations.quote: I relied on a study conducted at Emory University (published by Schuster et al, *J Urol* 191: 1446-1453, 2014) for the primary evidence of efficacy
Study BED001 was the sponsor's re-analysis of imaging data from the previously conducted R01 study at Emory University.

Study R01 was an open label, single dose comparative study of ^{18}F-Fluciclovine vs. ^{123}I-Prostascint with histology as a standard of truth and was performed at Emory University; it was published in 2014 in *The Journal of Urology* (Vol. 191, 1446-1453, May 2014).

design.text: Open label, single center, non-randomized comparative study of 18F-Fluciclovine PET imaging with histology (biopsy) as the standard of truth

citations.quote: **Basic Design:** Open label, single center, non-randomized, comparative study of ^{18}F-Fluciclovine PET imaging vs. ^{123}I-Prostascint SPECT imaging in prostate cancer patients

population.text: Men with suspected recurrence of prostate cancer based on rising PSA levels following radical prostatectomy and/or radiotherapy

citations.quote: The efficacy of Axumin was evaluated in two studies in men with suspected recurrence of prostate cancer based on rising PSA levels following radical prostatectomy and/or radiotherapy.

endpoint.text: Positive Predictive Value (PPV) at subject, lesion and region level, validated against histopathology

citations.quote: **Primary Endpoints:** Positive Predictive Value (PPV) on a subject, lesion and region level for the prostate bed, pelvic lymph nodes and extra prostatic sites.

n.text: 105 Axumin scans evaluated in comparison to histopathology

citations.quote: The Emory study evaluated 105 Axumin scans in comparison to histopathology obtained by biopsy of the prostate bed and biopsies of lesions suspicious by imaging.

result.text: Study met its primary PPV endpoint; at the subject level 7 of 10 (71%) patients with lesions detected by fluciclovine F 18 had prostatic cancer metastases and nearly all (97%) patients with metastases had detections verified as positive by histology

citations.quote: The study met its primary efficacy endpoint of positive predictive value and these results were consistent with multiple additional analyses of performance.

At the subject level seven of ten patients with lesions detected by Fluciclovine F18 (71%) had prostatic cancer metastases and nearly all (97%) patient with metastases had Fluciclovine F 18 detections verified as positive by histology.

indication.text: Radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for PET imaging in men with suspected prostate cancer recurrence based on elevated blood PSA levels following prior treatment

citations.quote: Axumin is a radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging in men with suspected prostate cancer recurrence based on elevated blood prostate specific antigen (PSA) levels following prior treatment (1).

target_moa.text: Fluciclovine F 18 is a synthetic amino acid taken up across cell membranes by amino acid transporters (LAT-1 and ASCT2) that are upregulated in prostate cancer cells, resulting in greater uptake in prostate cancer cells than in surrounding normal tissue; detected by PET

citations.quote: Fluciclovine F 18 is a synthetic amino acid transported across mammalian cell membranes by amino acid transporters, such as LAT-1 and ASCT2, which are upregulated in prostate cancer cells. Fluciclovine F 18 is taken up to a greater extent in prostate cancer cells compared with surrounding normal tissues.

modality.text: Radiopharmaceutical (F-18 labeled synthetic amino acid analog)

citations.quote: Axumin contains the fluorine 18 (F 18) labeled synthetic amino acid analog fluciclovine. Fluciclovine F 18 is a radioactive diagnostic agent used with PET imaging.

key_safety.text: Adverse reactions were reported in <=1% of subjects; most common were injection site pain, injection site erythema and dysgeusia. No deaths or serious adverse reactions were reported.

citations.quote: Adverse reactions were reported in \le 1\% of subjects during clinical studies with Axumin. The most common adverse reactions were injection site pain, injection site erythema and dysgeusia.
No deaths or serious adverse reactions were reported. Adverse reactions occurred in <1% study subjects. The most common were injection site pain and dysgeusia.

detail.text: DRISK determined a REMS was not necessary; as a class diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals have not required a REMS, and the applicant did not submit a proposed REMS

citations.quote: As a class, diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals have not required a REMS for approval. The applicant did not submit a proposed REMS or risk management plan wit

vote.text: No advisory committee meeting was held; the application did not raise regulatory or scientific issues and there was regulatory precedent (Choline C 11)

citations.quote: The application did not raise regulatory or scientific issues. The approval of another radiopharmaceutical (Choline C 11) was based on similar study design and endpoint (lesion localization rates verified by histopathology) in the same patient population (patients with elevated PSA levels suspected of cancer recurrence). For these reasons no advisory committee meeting was necessary.

detail.text: Application submitted September 28, 2015 and approved effective on the date of the approval letter; no prior CRL indicated

citations.quote: We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling text.

Please refer to the New Drug Application (NDA) dated and received September 28, 2015, and your amendments, submitted under 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Axumin (fluciclovine F 18) injection, 335-8200 MBq/mL (9-221 mCi/mL).

basis.text: Granted priority review because fluciclovine F 18 was judged to have the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy for a serious condition for which accurate diagnosis is critical for patient management and improved outcome

citations.quote: The application was granted a priority review status because Fluciclovine F 18 was judged to have the potential to improve the diagnostic accuracy for a serious condition for which an accurate diagnosis is critical for patient management and improved outcome.

summary.text: New molecular entity diagnostic radiopharmaceutical submitted by Blue Earth Diagnostics on September 28, 2015 and granted priority review; approved without an advisory committee meeting and without a REMS. It was a traditional (non-accelerated) approval based on an Emory University study meeting its primary PPV endpoint.

citations.quote: On September 28, 2015 the Applicant (Blue Earth Diagnostics Ltd) submitted a 505(b)(1) new drug application (NDA) for the new molecular entity Fluciclovine F 18.

The application was granted a priority review status because Fluciclovine F 18 was judged to have the potential to improve the diagnostic accuracy for a serious condition for which an accurate diagnosis is critical for patient management and improved outcome.
